dataScale.title: [pt] Scale and storage (honest)
dataScale.lead: [pt] Recording is sparse by design — not every game tick becomes a row — but gzip SDK samples add up when you drive for months. Folding in Archive only collapses what you see in the timeline; it does not delete history on disk.
dataScale.ingestBody: [pt] default about one second between eligible rows, plus writes when speed or job context changes, on collisions, or at job boundaries.
dataScale.foldBody: [pt] collapse adjacent snapshots in the same minute (or second/hour) when route, cargo, truck, trailer, speed, and on-job match; fines and deliveries always stay visible.
dataScale.sizeBody: [pt] on the order of half a megabyte per thousand stored observations for list data; with full inspector samples, often a few kilobytes per row — expect single-digit to low tens of gigabytes for multi-million-mile careers unless you tune sampling.
dataScale.hotBody: [pt] recent facts stay in SQLite; older observations can move to cold column files and a search index so the console stays responsive.
dataScale.quotaBody: [pt] the app does not enforce a disk cap; use Settings maintenance, vault export, and mock purge when a folder grows past what your disk comfortably holds.

catalog.archiveFoldSimilar: [pt] Fold similar — collapse matching snapshots in a time window; fines and deliveries never fold
catalog.ldpArchitectureLayer: [pt] Hot ledger, cold column files, and search index on one machine — sparse ingest and rollup buckets keep dashboards fast as observation counts climb into the millions.

arrowIpc.title: [pt] Arrow IPC
arrowIpc.body: [pt] Column-oriented tables streamed between processes in a compact binary format.
arrowIpc.layman: [pt] A wide pipe that moves spreadsheet-style columns in bulk.
arrowIpc.ol: [pt] Desktop archive uses this for large timeline windows.

sse.title: [pt] Server-Sent Events (SSE)
sse.body: [pt] A one-way HTTP channel where the server pushes live updates to the browser.
sse.layman: [pt] Overlay pages keep a light connection open for fresh numbers.
sse.ol: [pt] Panel URLs subscribe for live speed, job, and compose widgets.

mmf.title: [pt] Memory-mapped file (MMF)
mmf.body: [pt] On Windows, shared RAM the game plugin and Overlane both map into.
mmf.layman: [pt] A shared clipboard both the game and Overlane read instantly.
mmf.ol: [pt] Official path uses Local\OverlaneTelemetry via overlane-telemetry.dll.

duckdb.title: [pt] DuckDB
duckdb.body: [pt] Embedded analytical SQL for local files without a separate database server.
duckdb.layman: [pt] SQL analytics on your trip files on disk.
duckdb.ol: [pt] Shipped in Windows installers for archive viewports and rollups.

tantivy.title: [pt] Tantivy
tantivy.body: [pt] Full-text search engine for fast keyword queries over archive text.
tantivy.ol: [pt] Indexes journal and archive text on your machine.

parquet.title: [pt] Apache Parquet
parquet.body: [pt] Compressed columnar files suited to cold historical facts.
parquet.layman: [pt] Efficient packing for older trips on disk.
parquet.ol: [pt] Cold tier storage for archived observations.

sqlite.title: [pt] SQLite
sqlite.body: [pt] Embedded SQL database used as the hot ledger for recent observations.
sqlite.layman: [pt] Today's drive notes land here first.
sqlite.ol: [pt] Live telemetry does not write here; ingest does when recording is on.

wal.title: [pt] SQLite WAL
wal.body: [pt] Write-ahead logging for safer concurrent reads and writes.
wal.layman: [pt] Browse the archive while new rows still land.
wal.ol: [pt] Hot ledger mode for ingest overlap.

zstd.title: [pt] ZSTD
zstd.body: [pt] Modern compression for smaller cold files.
zstd.layman: [pt] Tighter packing so disks fill slower.
zstd.ol: [pt] Used when tiering observations to cold storage.

fts.title: [pt] Full-text search (FTS)
fts.body: [pt] Inverted index for keyword search without scanning every row.
fts.layman: [pt] The lookup table behind archive search.
fts.ol: [pt] Works with filters like @cargo: in the console.

clad.title: [pt] CLAD
clad.body: [pt] Composable Layered Agnostic Design — small units wired through explicit interfaces.
clad.layman: [pt] Labeled blocks instead of one tangled script.
clad.ol: [pt] How this marketing site and the product UI stay modular.

nsis.title: [pt] NSIS
nsis.body: [pt] Windows installer technology used for Overlane setup bundles.
nsis.layman: [pt] The familiar Next → Next installer wizard.
nsis.ol: [pt] Production and Demo are separate downloads.

tauri.title: [pt] Tauri
tauri.body: [pt] Native Windows shell hosting the web console and user-session telemetry worker lifecycle.
tauri.layman: [pt] The desktop app wrapper around the browser console.
tauri.ol: [pt] Boot splash, health-gated startup, bundled telemetry DLL — worker is not a Windows service.

loopback.title: [pt] Loopback bind
loopback.body: [pt] HTTP listens on localhost unless you opt into LAN exposure in Settings.
loopback.layman: [pt] Overlane talks on your PC by default—not the whole café Wi‑Fi.
loopback.ol: [pt] Default for console and overlay URLs.

sidecar.title: [pt] Telemetry worker
sidecar.body: [pt] Companion Go process for API, live feed, ingest, and archive — runs in your user session, not as a Windows service.
sidecar.layman: [pt] The engine running while the desktop window is open.
sidecar.ol: [pt] Started by the desktop app at launch; exits when you quit Overlane.

spa.title: [pt] Single-page app (SPA)
spa.body: [pt] Web UI that swaps views without full page reloads.
spa.layman: [pt] One window; hop between Archive, Journal, Settings.

scsSdk.title: [pt] SCS SDK
scsSdk.body: [pt] Official plugin SDK for ETS2 and ATS telemetry.
scsSdk.layman: [pt] The hook that reads what the truck is doing in-game.

oltp.title: [pt] OLTP
oltp.body: [pt] Many small, fast writes as you drive.
oltp.layman: [pt] Recording each moment as it happens.

gettingStarted.title: [pt] Getting started
gettingStarted.lead: [pt] Overlane runs on your PC. Nothing is uploaded off your machine by default.
gettingStarted.b0: [pt] Get the latest production NSIS installer from https://short.army/overlane (hero Download button or sticky Buy now).
gettingStarted.b1: [pt] Run the installer — per-user, not a Windows service — and start Overlane from the Start menu or tray.
gettingStarted.b2: [pt] Follow the game-link wizard: pick your ETS2 or ATS folder and install the official telemetry plugin when prompted.
gettingStarted.b3: [pt] Open Overlays and copy a panel URL into OBS or a browser beside the game.
gettingStarted.b4: [pt] Optional: enable recording under Settings → Storage for archive timelines, dashboard rollups, and search.

playerGuide.title: [pt] Player guide
playerGuide.lead0: [pt] You need a supported telemetry plugin in the game’s plugins folder and the Overlane Windows app.
playerGuide.b0: [pt] Load a profile in the game — the console health strip shows when telemetry is live.
playerGuide.b1: [pt] Open Home for the Live driving card: speed, fuel, gear, odometer, and active route when you are on a job.
playerGuide.b2: [pt] Use Overlays to copy panel URLs into your streaming app.
playerGuide.b3: [pt] Tray menu: open the console or quit before running an installer upgrade.
playerGuide.b4: [pt] Overlane Demo ships mock telemetry and sample archive data — console, overlays, archive, and journal work with no game.
